criteria_results.title: Identifies breach notification timing gap (72 hrs vs 24 hrs)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-19 flags 72 hours from confirmation under § 7.1 vs the Playbook 24-hour requirement.

criteria_results.title: Identifies breach notification trigger threshold difference
criteria_results.reasoning: D-19 identifies the 'confirmation' trigger vs the required confirmed-or-suspected/discovery trigger.

criteria_results.title: Identifies sub-processor notice period gap (15 days vs 30 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-07 flags § 5.2 15 calendar days' notice vs the required 30 days.

criteria_results.title: Identifies sub-processor objection right nullification
criteria_results.reasoning: D-08 flags that Processor 'may proceed ... at its discretion' over an unresolved objection, with no termination remedy.

criteria_results.title: Identifies compressed sub-processor objection window
criteria_results.reasoning: D-08 notes the 10-day objection window makes the right illusory.

criteria_results.title: Identifies sub-processor liability limitation
criteria_results.reasoning: D-10 flags § 5.5 'commercially reasonable efforts to remediate' vs full liability for sub-processors.

criteria_results.title: Identifies audit rights deviation: default is questionnaire, not on-site
criteria_results.reasoning: D-25 flags questionnaire/SOC 2 at Processor's election with on-site audit only if insufficient, vs a primary on-site and remote audit right.

criteria_results.title: Identifies audit rights deviation: 45 days notice vs 15 business days
criteria_results.reasoning: D-27 flags 45 days' notice vs the 15-business-day requirement.

criteria_results.title: Identifies audit rights deviation: once every 24 months vs annual
criteria_results.reasoning: D-27 flags once every 24 months vs annual frequency.

criteria_results.title: Identifies audit rights deviation: cost allocation
criteria_results.reasoning: D-26 flags Controller bearing all costs including Processor internal costs vs the no-charge requirement.

criteria_results.title: Identifies data deletion timeline gap (90 days vs 30 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-29 flags 90 calendar days vs the 30-day requirement.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing written certification of deletion
criteria_results.reasoning: D-30 flags that there is no certification of deletion and asks for one within 10 business days.

criteria_results.title: Identifies indefinite retention of de-identified/aggregated data
criteria_results.reasoning: D-31 flags § 11.3 indefinite retention of de-identified/aggregated data for product improvement and benchmarking.

criteria_results.title: Identifies liability cap gap ($1.92M vs $5.76M minimum)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-33 identifies the roughly 1x annual fee cap against the $1,920,000 ACV illustration and a 3x floor of $5,760,000, so the cap is one-third of the minimum.

criteria_results.title: Notes Playbook preference for uncapped liability for data breaches
criteria_results.reasoning: D-33 sets uncapped liability as the primary position and the 3x ACV super-cap as the fallback floor.

criteria_results.title: Identifies insurance per-occurrence shortfall ($5M vs $10M)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-35 identifies $5M per occurrence vs the required $10M (half the requirement).

criteria_results.title: Identifies insurance aggregate shortfall ($10M vs $20M)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-35 identifies $10M aggregate vs the required $20M.

criteria_results.title: Identifies cross-border transfer without prior written consent
criteria_results.reasoning: D-24 flags § 8.2 transfers for DR, load balancing and sub-processor operations without consent or required SCCs.

criteria_results.title: Identifies undisclosed Irish subsidiary of Redline Analytics
criteria_results.reasoning: The report flags Redline's 'international infrastructure' but never identifies the Irish subsidiary, Redline Analytics Europe Ltd.

criteria_results.title: Connects undisclosed Irish subsidiary to cross-border transfer risk
criteria_results.reasoning: The Irish subsidiary is never identified, so it is not linked to cross-border transfer risk.

criteria_results.title: Identifies HIPAA disclosure record retention gap (3 years vs 6 years)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-38 flags 3-year disclosure records vs 6 years under 45 CFR § 164.528(a)(1) as a regulatory defect.

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing explicit minimum necessary provision in BAA
criteria_results.reasoning: D-37 flags B.2.1 'only as permitted' language and the missing explicit minimum-necessary clause under § 164.502(b).

criteria_results.title: Identifies missing HITECH Act breach notification reference in BAA
criteria_results.reasoning: D-39 flags that there is no 42 USC § 17932 breach-notification reference in the BAA.

criteria_results.title: Identifies narrow Security Incident definition
criteria_results.reasoning: D-01 flags § 1.12 as confirmed-only with an exclusion of unsuccessful attempts, vs confirmed-or-suspected.

criteria_results.title: Identifies data subject rights response timeline gap (15 vs 5 days)
criteria_results.reasoning: D-22 flags 15 business days vs the 5-business-day standard.

criteria_results.title: Identifies absence of documented instructions mechanism
criteria_results.reasoning: D-04 flags 'complete and exclusive instructions' with no supplemental-instruction mechanism.

criteria_results.title: Identifies BAA de-identification right permitting unrestricted use of de-identified PHI
criteria_results.reasoning: D-40 flags B.2.4 de-identification 'without restriction' and its commercial-use concerns; D-31 notes re-identification risk for the 1.4M-record dataset.

criteria_results.title: Each deviation includes a risk severity rating
criteria_results.reasoning: Every deviation has a Critical/High/Medium/Low severity rating.

criteria_results.title: Each deviation cites specific DPA provision and Playbook/Checklist requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: Nearly all deviations cite a DPA/Exhibit section and a Playbook Req. or BAA checklist number.

criteria_results.title: Each deviation includes a primary redline recommendation
criteria_results.reasoning: Each deviation has a concrete 'Ask' with specific contractual terms.

criteria_results.title: Each deviation includes a fallback position distinct from primary
criteria_results.reasoning: Many deviations (e.g., D-09, D-11, D-13, D-20, D-26, D-30, D-37 to D-39, D-41 to D-46) have no fallback or say 'none'; well under 75% have a distinct fallback.

criteria_results.title: Breach notification rated Critical or High severity
criteria_results.reasoning: Breach notification D-19 is rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap deviation rated Critical or High severity
criteria_results.reasoning: Liability cap D-33 is rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: HIPAA disclosure retention rated Critical or High severity
criteria_results.reasoning: HIPAA disclosure retention D-38 is rated Critical.

criteria_results.title: Encryption at rest standard gap: missing AES-256 specification
criteria_results.reasoning: D-12 flags that no named standard (AES-256) is specified for at-rest encryption.

criteria_results.title: Encryption at rest gap: backup encryption qualified by 'technically feasible'
criteria_results.reasoning: D-12 flags backups encrypted only 'where technically feasible' and treats it as a walk-away point.

criteria_results.title: Notes expired HITRUST certification as a concern
criteria_results.reasoning: D-14 and Section 4 flag the HITRUST r2 re-certification as pending and a possible lapse requiring follow-up; the Feb 28, 2025 date itself is not stated.

criteria_results.title: Liability cap redline proposes uncapped or 3x ACV as fallback
criteria_results.reasoning: D-33 proposes uncapped liability as primary and a 3x ACV ($5.76M) floor as fallback.

criteria_results.title: Sub-processor objection right redline proposes termination right
criteria_results.reasoning: D-08 asks for a no-penalty termination right if the objection is unresolved within 30 days.

criteria_results.title: Report identifies the transmittal email as source for Irish subsidiary
criteria_results.reasoning: The report cites Kessler's transmittal email saying Redline uses 'international infrastructure' as evidence of undisclosed non-U.S. processing.

criteria_results.title: Report correctly identifies the number of patient records at stake
criteria_results.reasoning: The report references about 1.4 million patient-users to frame severity.
